clips.title: Introduction to the Prometheus Monitoring System | Key Concepts and Features
clips.why: One of Prometheus's creators explains its data model and the text format a service shows on /metrics.
look: A series is a metric name plus labels, with timestamped values.
The text format: HELP and TYPE lines, then one line per series.
Labels are how you split one metric into many series, which is also why they must stay few.
clips.after: The gateway's /metrics page is exactly this format, with agent, step and type as labels.

clips.title: Understanding Prometheus Metric Types | Meaning and Usage (Gauge, Counter, Summary, Histogram)
clips.why: What a counter is, what happens when it resets, and why you query rates instead of raw values.
look: A counter only goes up, and resets to zero when the process restarts.
inc() with an amount, the way the gateway adds a call's tokens.
The absolute value of a counter is rarely useful; rate() is.
clips.after: That is why the gateway never computes a rate itself: it counts, and VictoriaMetrics answers "per second" over any window.

clips.title: Understanding Prometheus Metric Types | Meaning and Usage (Gauge, Counter, Summary, Histogram)
clips.why: How a histogram stores durations in cumulative buckets, and how histogram_quantile() turns them into percentiles.
look: Buckets are cumulative: each one counts everything at or below its limit.
The _bucket, _sum and _count lines, as on the gateway's page.
histogram_quantile() estimates a percentile from bucket rates.
clips.after: In the lab, the same query showed a median of about 2 seconds and a p95 of about 22, which no average would show.

clips.title: How Prometheus Monitoring works | Prometheus Architecture explained
clips.why: Why Prometheus pulls, and the one case where pushing is the right answer: jobs that do not live long enough to be scraped.
look: With pull, a target that stops answering is itself a signal.
Short-lived jobs cannot wait for the scraper.
Prometheus's own answer is a Pushgateway; VictoriaMetrics simply accepts pushed lines on its import endpoint.
clips.after: Our services are scraped by VMAgent, and the nightly metrics job pushes, so both kinds meet in the same database.

practice.q: Finish the line so the counter grows by the call's real number of input tokens.
practice.why: inc(labels, amount) adds the amount. A counter has no set() and never goes down.

practice.q: The bucket lines say le="1" 3, le="5" 9, le="30" 10. How many calls took more than 5 seconds?

options.why: Buckets are cumulative: 10 calls in all, 9 at 5 seconds or less, so 1 took longer.
10 is every call at 30 seconds or less, which is all of them.
That is the number between 1 and 5 seconds (9 minus 3), not above 5.

practice.q: Finish the query that turns the token counter into tokens per second over the last minute.
practice.hint: The function that also handles counter resets.
practice.why: rate() computes the per-second growth of a counter over the window and treats a drop to zero as a restart.

practice.q: Put the life of one number in order, from a model call to a dashboard.
items: A model call finishes in the gateway
The gateway calls tokens.inc() and callSeconds.observe()
VMAgent reads /metrics on its next scrape and stores the values
A dashboard asks for rate() and histogram_quantile() over a window
VictoriaMetrics answers with per-second rates and percentiles
practice.why: The service only counts. Storing and computing happen on the database side, after the scrape.

practice.q: Which program should push its numbers instead of being scraped?

options.text: The LLM gateway, because it handles many calls
options.why: A busy, long-running service is the ideal case for pull.

options.text: The nightly delivery-metrics job that runs for two minutes
options.why: It is not running when the scraper comes, so it pushes once, with timestamps, and exits.

options.text: The broker, because it holds credentials
options.why: Holding credentials has nothing to do with it. The broker is a long-running service and is scraped.
